n: David begins with trust and asks God, who always does what is right, to rescue him so his faith is never put to shame.

f.g: God’s righteousness here means his faithfulness to rescue those in covenant with him.

n: Like a person leaning down to hear a quiet voice, God is asked to bend close and act quickly. David wants God to be his fortress.

f.g: A tender idiom: lean in to listen.
A fortress or stronghold.

n: Since God already is his rock and fortress, David asks him to lead and guide him — not because David deserves it, but because it fits God’s own name and character.

f.g: For the honor of God’s character and reputation.

n: His enemies have secretly set a trap. David asks God to pull him free, since God is his strength.

f.g: Secretly.

n: David entrusts his very life into God’s hands. Jesus spoke these words on the cross as he died, making this verse a perfect picture of trust in the Father.

f.w: Into thine hand I commit my spirit

f.g: Ransomed, rescued.

n: David rejects people who devote themselves to worthless idols. His trust is in the Lord alone.

f.g: Worthless idols — empty things that cannot help.

n: He rejoices in God’s loyal love because God has truly seen his troubles and known him personally in hard times.

f.w: thou hast known my soul in adversities
f.g: God cares for and understands him in his distress.

n: Instead of trapping him in the enemy’s grip, God set him in an open, spacious place where he could move freely.

f.g: A broad, open place — the opposite of being hemmed in.

n: Now a lament begins. David’s grief affects him eyes to stomach — his whole body aches with sorrow.

f.g: The body or inner being; grief felt physically.

n: Years of sorrow have worn him down. David admits some of his weakness comes from his own sin, and he feels it even in his bones.

f.g: Wasted away — a picture of deep exhaustion in body and spirit.

n: Enemies mock him, neighbors shame him, and acquaintances avoid him — people cross the street rather than meet him. Isolation adds to his pain.

f.g: An object of scorn or disgrace.

f.w: they that did see me without fled from me
f.g: Those who saw him outside, in the street, ran away from him.

n: He feels forgotten like the dead and as useless as a smashed clay jar. These are honest words of depression, and the Psalms make room for them.

f.g: A shattered pot, worthless and thrown away.

n: Rumors swirl and terror is everywhere as his enemies plot to kill him. Jeremiah later used the same phrase, “fear on every side.”
“But I trusted” — the turning point. In the middle of the storm, David holds onto one simple confession: you are my God.
All the moments and seasons of his life are in God’s hands, not the enemy’s. This is a quiet statement that God, not chance, governs his life.

f.w: My times are in thy hand

n: David asks God to smile on him, echoing the priestly blessing. A shining face means favor and approval.
He asks that his trust not end in disappointment, and that the wicked be the ones silenced — sent quiet to the grave.

f.g: Hebrew Sheol, the realm of the dead.

n: David prays that arrogant, lying mouths that insult the righteous would be shut.

f.g: Insolent, hard, arrogant words.

n: An outburst of wonder: God has goodness stored up like treasure for those who reverence him, and he shows it openly before others.

f.g: Stored away like treasure.

n: God hides his people in the safety of his presence, sheltering them from human pride and from quarrelsome, wounding speech.

f.g: Disputes, accusations and harmful words.
A shelter or booth.

n: David blesses the Lord, who showed him wonderful loyal love — as if placing him inside a fortified city.

f.g: A walled, fortified city; possibly recalling a real refuge such as Keilah.

n: David confesses that in his panic he concluded God had cut him off. Yet God heard him anyway. Our fears don’t limit God’s hearing.

f.g: In my alarm or panic.

n: He calls all the faithful to love the Lord, who protects the loyal and fully repays the proud.

f.g: Hebrew ḥasidim — the faithful covenant people.
Pays back in full those who act arrogantly.

n: The psalm closes with encouragement to all who hope in the Lord: take heart, and he will make you strong.
